text: Version 3 of the audit and logging design is issued as Draft. No approval of the source version and no approval of this version is recorded in any source read by this work package.
why: The run records no human approval; a missing approval is treated as an assumption and the document continues in Draft rather than stopping.
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.1 and the realignment overlay D-RCV-60 (a missing status is an assumption, not a stop).
confirm: The document owner confirms or records the approval of version 3.
impact: Documentation only; nothing is built from an unapproved status.

text: The file name gives the version of the family and the metadata table gives the document's own issue number. The source is therefore version 2 of the family and version 1 of its own table, and this document is version 3. The source values are kept in a 'Source version' row as 1, 28 October 2026.
why: The source file is named v2 while its table reads version 1 and the core properties read revision 1; one reading must be chosen so that the next version has a number and the change log a row.
read: Source metadata table rows 'Version | 1' and 'Date | 28 October 2026'; source file name 'Recovery Workbench Audit and Logging Design v2.docx'; Template and Rules v1 R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1).
applied_in: Metadata table, Version, Date and Source version rows; change log
confirm: The document owner confirms the version numbering of the family.
impact: One change-log row and one metadata row; no content depends on it.

text: The arc42 crosscutting-concepts structure of the source is kept. Sections 1 to 6 stay in their order and keep their numbers, and three sections are added at the end: 7 Owners and contracts, 8 Decisions, and 9 Realignment changes in version 3.
why: The realignment needs an owner table, a decision table and a change table, and the source has no place for them; renumbering the source sections would break every reference to them.
read: Source sections 1 to 6 and its metadata row 'Structure | arc42 crosscutting concepts, C4 component view'; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 to R8.3.
confirm: The document owner accepts the added sections.
impact: Three added sections; no section is renumbered.

text: The local decision record is one table in the schema of the service that takes the decision, written through the decision-record library in the same transaction as the state change and the outbox row. Its name and DDL are left to the DB story of each service. It carries chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash and entry_hash, and the case reference and the trace ID travel in inputsRef.
why: Architecture v5 requires the record and gives no table, no DDL and no case column, while the field list of the Temporal and Drools design has to be carried somewhere; the field list is used as written and the case and trace references are placed in the reference field.
read: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28; Temporal and Drools Design v1 decision record field list; source sections 2 and 3; Ownership Map v1 (no local record table).
applied_in: Section 2.1; section 7 table, decision record row
confirm: The service owners and P7 confirm the field list, the table name and the placement of the case reference.
impact: Every service's DB story creates one table and its migration; no business value changes.

text: The access log is an append-only store in rwb_access, owned by P4 rwb-access, read through GET /admin/access-log and written inside the same transaction as the access decision.
why: The source puts the access log inside the decision log store, the Ownership Map gives the read API to P4 and lists no access-log table; placing it with the service that owns the rights keeps one writer.
read: Source section 1 access log row and section 4 insert-only rule; ownership.json api 'GET /admin/access-log' with owner P4; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet (no access_log row).
applied_in: Section 1 access log row; section 7 table
confirm: P4 confirms the store and the DB story creates it.
impact: One table and its migration in rwb_access; the decision log store no longer holds it.

text: The central ledger is the table decision_log_entry of schema rwb_decision, owned by P7 rwb-decision, fed idempotently from topic rwb.decision-record.v1 (EV-08) and read through GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId}.
why: The Ownership Map and the plan ownership file give decision_log_entry and both endpoints to P7 and Architecture v5 gives P7 the central decision ledger and the daily seal.
read: ownership.json tables decision_log_entry (P7) and api GET /decision-log (P7); Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb_decision: approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry; immutable storage for the daily ledger seal); slide 42 EV-08.
applied_in: Section 1 decision log row; section 3; section 4; section 7 table
confirm: P7 confirms the table and the read paths.
impact: One writer of the ledger, 19 producers of the event.

text: The interaction ledger stays with P1 rwb-source-data (tables interaction and efs_ledger_outcome) and rwb-case reads it through the P1 contract, as the plan default ruling and DP-18 say.
why: The source names no owner, the plan default ruling and DP-18 place the ledger in P1, and the latest module specifications still place the table and the endpoints in P3; one owner must be recorded.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-18; ownership.json rulings for interaction and efs_ledger_outcome (P1); TSD P3 v3 T3.1 and API Specification v4 x-module P3 (the conflicting reading).
applied_in: Section 1 interaction ledger row; section 7 table
confirm: P1 and P3 confirm the contract direction in the wave 1 integration story.
impact: One writer and one read contract; rwb-case keeps its screen and calls P1.

text: The nightly copy of the decision log to the data lake is removed. It is replaced by the continuous ingest JOB-13 in rwb-decision and by the daily ledger seal to write-once storage. RWB-E1-014 is retired and its dependencies are dropped.
why: Architecture v5 has no data lake, removes INT-19 and INT-20, and makes the ingest continuous with a daily seal; the source and the previous batch design still describe the nightly copy.
read: Architecture v5 slide 37 (no data lake), slide 14 (daily ledger seal, WORM) and slide 44 (JOB-13, JOB-14); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired).
applied_in: Section 1 decision log row; section 4; section 8
confirm: P7 confirms that no archive job outside rwb-decision replaces the copy.
impact: One job removed, one job redefined; no reporting read depends on the lake copy.

text: Every retention period of the source is kept as written under DL26. Where each period is held and which job enforces it is left open: the retention tables of the map are rwb-document (P5) and JOB-17 is document retention, so the ledger and access-log periods need their own rows, owned by P7, P1 and P4.
why: The source gives the periods but the target has no retention table for the ledgers and the access log, and the only retention tables in the map belong to documents.
read: Source section 5 table; ownership.json tables retention_rule and retention_action (P5) and jobs JOB-17 (P5); Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44.
confirm: Compliance states where the three periods are held and which job enforces them.
impact: No period changes; three stories add a retention row and a check.

text: Each service chains its own decision records in chain_seq order, starting from an empty prev_hash; the central ledger chains its entries again on ingest, and the daily WORM fingerprint covers the ledger chain. The ledger chain is the chain of record for an auditor, and the local chain is available for a replay of one service.
why: Architecture v5 describes a chain in each service and a chain verification plus a daily anchor in the ledger, and names no scope for either; two chains need one rule so that a break can be reported.
read: Architecture v5 slide 28 (hash-linked locally, chain verification, daily anchor to WORM); Temporal and Drools Design v1 (chain_seq, prev_hash, entry_hash); source section 4.
confirm: P7 and Internal Audit confirm the chain of record and the first-record rule.
impact: Two chain checks and one daily seal per environment.

text: The approver of a decision is stored as an identifier, never as a name. The identifier is masked in every export under the masking rows of rwb-access and every read of the field is recorded in the PII log.
why: The source records 'who decided' and forbids personal fields in logs, and the target field is a user identifier; an identifier is personal data under PDPA, so the reading has to say how it is exposed.
read: Source section 2 decided_by row and section 6; Temporal and Drools Design v1 approverUserId; Architecture v5 slides 30 and 35 (audit and PII access logs to SOC); E1-037.
confirm: Compliance and Information Security confirm the protection of the column and the mask.
impact: One mask row in rwb-access and one PII-log event per read; no decision rule changes.

text: Every owner in this document is a service code of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 or the platform (PLT), never a team type and never a person. Where the source names a component that the map does not own, as with the ACE Common logging and the SOC log, the document names the party outside the 19 services and the contract that reaches it.
why: The WP requires the Ownership Map for every owner and AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids names of people; the source names readers by role and names no service at all.
read: Microservice Ownership Map v1 (Read me, Services, Tables, Endpoints, Workflows and activities, Rulings); plan ownership.json; AGENTS.md rule 4.
confirm: No confirmation needed; the map is the ruling.
impact: Every owner is traceable to a map row.

text: A decision record, a Kafka event and a workflow input carry references and never a copy of personal data, and a payload is encrypted by the codec before it leaves the service. Personal data reaches the SOC only through the ACE PII Kafka path.
why: The source forbids personal fields in logs and prompts, and the target now moves the record as an event and through a workflow, so the same rule has to be stated for the two new carriers.
read: Source section 2 inputs row and section 6; Architecture v5 slide 20 (outbox and DecisionRecorded), slide 28 (record and state change in one transaction), slide 30 (audit and PII logging through ACE) and slide 35; ADR-015, ADR-016.
confirm: No confirmation needed; the rule is the source rule applied to the new carriers.
impact: Every event and workflow payload is reviewed for personal data before the story is Done.

text: No date of the source is moved and no release date is added. The source date of 28 October 2026 is kept as the source version date, and a date later read as a release is tentative (U7, DL48).
why: The source carries no release date and the run fixes dates as unchanged and tentative; a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules v1 R1 U7 and R8.4 (DL48); AGENTS.md rules 10 and the WP instruction that release dates get '(tentative)'.
applied_in: Metadata table, Source version row; section 8
impact: None; the document carries no release date at all.

text: The core properties of the new file are set to the organisation and the tool: author 'Henka Group', last modified by 'T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash', title 'Recovery Workbench Audit and Logging Design v3', revision 3. The source file carries a person name in author and last modified by, which an output may not carry.
why: AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids names of people anywhere, and the source document properties hold one; the new file therefore rewrites the four properties.
read: Source core properties (author and last modified by hold a person name, revision 1); AGENTS.md rule 4; Template and Rules v1 R8.1.
applied_in: Document properties of the .docx (not visible in the body)
impact: Properties only; the source file is unchanged.

text: While the ledger lags, the local record is authoritative for the audit trail and the ledger entry is shown as not yet sealed; the audit search of section 3 reads the ledger only, and a strict-mode step waits for the acknowledgement of its own record only.
why: Architecture v5 gives the ledger a five-minute completeness target and gap alerts, and the source requires a search; no source states what a search returns for a committed record that is not yet sealed.
read: Architecture v5 slide 28 (five-minute target, gap alerts, strict mode at the points of no return); source section 3 (search and export) and section 4 (failed write raises an incident).
confirm: P7 and Internal Audit confirm the pending state and the search behaviour.
impact: One status on the ledger entry and one rule for strict mode.

text: The access log records the rule and model versions that the owning service applied at the time of the event, and the registry in rwb-decision (P7) stays the source of the version and its effective date. P4 writes the access row; it does not read the registry on the hot path.
why: The source requires 'versions in force' in the access log, the versions live in the P7 registry and are loaded by each service, and the access log is written in P4, so the writer has to be named.
read: Source section 1 access log row; Architecture v5 slide 14 (P7 rule registry) and slide 41 (P4 access); Temporal and Drools Design v1 (RulePackageInForce, EV-30, and the version written into the decision record).
confirm: P4 and P7 confirm the field and its writer.
impact: One field in the access row; no call from P4 to P7 on the hot path.
